candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Hymns on the Crucifixion
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Crucifixion IV.10-12 (NPNF S2 V13). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Hymns on the Crucifixion (c. 365 AD)

Aaron's rod swallowing the rods-turned-serpents of the magicians is, for Ephrem, an early figure of the Crucified Christ swallowing the dragon: the wood that becomes a serpent becomes a devouring serpent, and the devouring is itself the salvation. The Cross — wood that becomes the throne of the Serpent-conqueror — accomplishes in reality what the rod accomplished in type.

candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.19 (c. 350 AD)

'And the Lord said unto Moses, See, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet' — Athanasius marks dedōka se theon tō Pharaō (I have given thee as a god to Pharaoh) as the METHODOLOGICAL-KEY for the gods-by-participation vs theotēs-by-nature distinction. Moses is called 'god' by ECONOMIC-COMMUNICATION (his role-as-divine-mediator to Pharaoh) and by DIVINE-GRACIOUS-GRANT, not by nature. The Word, by contrast, is God by-nature (kata physin), not by-grace (kata charin); is-eternally-God, not-made-god. Athanasius pairs Exo 7:1 with Psa 82:6 ('I have said, Ye are gods'; cf. Jn 10:34) as the canonical-theōsis-by-grace pair, contrasting both with the Son's-deity-by-essence. Crucial anti-Arian hermeneutical-grid.
